about: Where app/agents/obs.js sends page views and reads. Public on purpose: an append token can only write to its lane, the key can only encrypt, and the read key reads the vault's published counts (stats/views.json), which hold nothing that is not on the site. Switched on 11 November 2026 at Dinis Cruz's word (the vault, the events' key and the public counts: his words of about 09:25 and 09:31 UTC in the observability session). The lanes' enum key and the events' private key are in a second, private vault held by the conductor; neither is in this repository. The place: at Dinis Cruz's word of about 09:47 UTC on 11 November (BRIEF.md, last section), app/agents/obs.js asks GeoJS (geo, below) once per tab session for the country and city; GeoJS sees the reader's IP address to answer; only the country code and city name are kept and sealed, never the IP address or anything finer.

geo.why_this_one: its terms allow any lawful, non-excessive use with no key and no account (no secret in the page), over HTTPS, answered to any origin (CORS); its privacy policy says it keeps no access logs, only error logs, and that its traffic passes through Cloudflare. Not chosen: ipapi.co (its terms forbid keeping a location beyond immediate use), DB-IP's free API (its FAQ says a browser needs a paid public key), ipwho.is (personal or internal use only)
geo.when: once per tab session, after the page has loaded, from storm-charles.promptugal.news only; never with Do Not Track, Global Privacy Control or Pause
geo.never_kept: the IP address, coordinates, region, postcode, time zone from the answer, network (ASN), organisation or provider name
geo.published: views by country; a city only with at least 5 views in the period, else counted as other in its country (data/agents/views.json, by_country)
